title: Audit logs & admin activity review with Crestwood Bank
summary: Review of Redwood audit logs and admin activity features: what is captured, export and streaming options (S3, syslog, SIEM), retention defaults and configurable policies, access controls for logs, encryption/KMS integration, and options to avoid storing sensitive prompt contents. Agreed next steps: send SOC 2/ISO artifacts, provide a scrubbed 30-day export sample, schedule SIEM integration workshop, and clarify retention SLA language for contract.
topics: what audit logs capture (admin login, role changes, API key events, model deploys, prompt/response metadata)
export options: S3 export, syslog, webhook, Kafka/Kinesis, Splunk/Datadog connectors
RBAC for log access and query UI
transcript:
Header: 2026-11-05 15:00 PST | Duration: 56m | Attendees: Maya, Jordan, Ravi - Redwood; Elena, Tom, Nora - Crestwood

00:00 Elena (CISO): okay thanks everyone for joining, we wanted to do a deep dive on audit logs and admin activity. primary concerns are retention, exportability to our SIEM, and making sure prompts or PII aren't leaked into logs.
00:18 Maya (Redwood AE): great, thanks Elena. quick intro — Jordan our solutions engineer will walk through the technical coverage; Ravi will handle ops/contract stuff. goal is to show what we capture, where logs live, and export/integration options.
00:32 Jordan (Redwood SE): yep hi all. quick note, I'll speak in terms of Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — some behaviors differ. for Hosted, by default we capture administrative events and system-level audit trails; for Dedicated and Private you get more control and can push logs to your infrastructure.
00:49 Tom (Platform Eng): when you say administrative events, give examples? like who changed RBAC, who created API keys, model rollouts etc?
00:56 Jordan: exactly — login events (sso/saml authn), role changes, user invites, API key creation/rotation/deletion, model deployment events (version, model id), route changes, and system alerts (failed deploys). we also capture request metadata for inference calls — timestamps, model id, token counts, response latency — but not full prompt text by default for hosted customers unless configured.
01:20 Nora (Compliance): "not by default" — can you confirm prompts are not stored in audit logs? we need to know where prompt content lives for data residency.
01:27 Jordan: yes, so there are two paths: operational logs and application payloads. operational audit logs do not contain full prompt text. we capture metadata about the request (request id, user id or api key id, model variant, token usage). if customers opt into full request logging for debugging or evals, that is stored in a separate request store and can be configured with retention and redaction.
01:46 Elena: and for our use case, we need those logs sent to our SIEM (we use Splunk) and also retained for 7 years for certain audit trails. what does Redwood support for export/long-term retention?
01:58 Jordan: we support several export/streaming mechanisms: periodic batch export to S3 (parquet/ndjson), real-time syslog/CEF forwarding, webhook or HTTP sink, and event streams via Kafka/Kinesis. we also have a Splunk HEC connector and documented guidance for Datadog/Elastic. retention on Hosted is default 90 days for operational audit logs; we offer extended retention as an add-on (custom tiers 1/3/7 years) and for Dedicated/Private customers you can configure infinite/long-term retention in your own storage.
02:28 Tom: are those exports encrypted in transit and at rest? and can they be encrypted with our KMS keys?
02:33 Jordan: yes, all exports use TLS, and files at rest in our S3 buckets are encrypted with AES-256. for Hosted we manage keys by default; we offer customer-managed KMS integration for Dedicated and Private, and for Hosted we can set up a Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) arrangement for certain enterprise contracts — it's handled through our KMS integration flow documented in the security pack.
02:56 Maya: i'll add we'll send the KMS integration guide after this call.
03:00 Elena: one concern: model outputs could contain customer data — are model responses ever captured in audit logs or exported by default?
03:08 Jordan: model responses are not included in the operational audit trail. as I mentioned, there's a separate request/interaction log used for debugging and quality monitoring. by default that store is disabled for Hosted customers; if enabled, it can be configured to redact or hash sensitive fields, or to never store the response body. for Private deployments it's your choice.
03:28 Nora: do you do automatic redaction? like detect credit card numbers, SSNs, PHI?
03:34 Jordan: we have optional PII scrubbing pipelines that run on request logs before export — regex-based plus ML-based detectors. customers can choose the scrubbing level: none, regex-only, or advanced ML-scrub with hashing/pseudonymization. we'll include the scrub rules doc.
03:49 Tom: on access controls, who at Redwood can see raw audit logs? we need RBAC and separation of duties — and we want the logs immutable once written.
03:59 Jordan: good Q. Access to audit logs is governed by RBAC. within Redwood, only staff with "security-read" or "support-ops" roles can access raw logs, and access requires Just-In-Time approval for sensitive exports. we maintain immutable append-only storage with write-once policies for compliance logs; we also support signed logs and tamper-evident hashing if you need cryptographic integrity.
04:23 Elena: can we get signed log digests daily and verify them on our side?
04:27 Jordan: yes, we can publish daily signed digests and a public key for verification. it's part of our enterprise audit integration.
04:34 Nora: how about audit trails for admin actions in the console — like who rolled back a model?
04:39 Jordan: console actions are included: user, timestamp, action (create/update/delete), resource id, before/after metadata where applicable. sometimes the "before/after" snapshots are truncated for size; we provide a change-diff field and a trace id you can use to fetch the full event if available.
04:55 Tom: what's the latency of streaming logs to our SIEM? near real-time?
04:59 Jordan: depends on the sink. syslog/HEC connectors are near real-time (sub-second to seconds), Kafka/Kinesis typical sub-second to low seconds. S3 exports are periodic (configurable, e.g., hourly or daily).
05:12 Elena: for regulatory retention we need writeable retention policies that prevent accidental deletion for 7 years. can Redwood enforce legal hold?
05:20 Jordan: on Hosted we have retention locks that can be part of your contract; they can be made immutable for the contract period. Dedicated/Private customers can enforce retention on their own storage. legal hold workflows require a support ticket with two approvers on the customer side and are logged as a sealed action.
05:37 Nora: audit logs will contain user identifiers. do you support hashing or PII tokenization for those identifiers before export?
05:44 Jordan: yes, we can hash or pseudonymize user IDs in the export pipeline; we usually include a reversible mapping stored in your KMS-protected vault if you need to re-identify for investigations. by default exports include raw user ids if permitted.
05:58 Customer (Tom): ok, a few practical asks — can you provide a sample export (30 days) for us to ingest into our Splunk? and can Jordan scrub any PII?
06:07 Maya: yes we'll do that. Jordan can generate a scrubbed sample and share an S3 link with temporary credentials.
06:13 Jordan: i'll pull a 30-day admin activity export and apply regex-based scrubbing to prompt and free-text fields, replace user emails with hashed identifiers. i'll target to have that by Monday.
06:22 Elena: also want to confirm logging of service account usage and API key rotations — we need an alert when a key is rotated or abused.
06:31 Jordan: we emit events for API key create/rotate/revoke and include the actor and IP address. we also have built-in anomaly detection that can surface unusual usage patterns; that can push to your alerting channel (webhook, PagerDuty, Splunk).
06:47 Nora: one more compliance question: do logs contain model inputs that might be considered PHI? what are best practices to avoid retaining PHI?
06:56 Jordan: best practice is to not enable full request logging for Hosted unless required; for PII/PHI workflows use Private or Dedicated with on-prem storage and enable scrubbing pipelines. we also recommend client-side redaction: mask or tokenise PHI before sending, and use per-request headers that mark content as sensitive to prevent logging.
07:18 Elena: okay that helps. can you confirm SOC 2 coverage of logs and if you have ISO 27001?
07:24 Maya: yes we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified — i'll attach the certs and our audit scope; note that some log retention options are contract-bound.
07:33 Elena: perfect. anything else on integrity or chain of custody?
07:37 Jordan: we support signed digests, tamper-evident chains, and export timestamps. we also provide an audit API to query events with verifiable timestamps.
07:48 Tom: about the audit API — is there rate limiting? we'd be doing bulk queries for incident response sometimes.
07:54 Jordan: there's a dedicated audit API with higher throughput tiers for enterprise; we can enable higher rate limits for your account under a service plan.
08:05 Nora: what about retention in EU regions? our data residency policy requires logs stored in EU for EU customers.
08:12 Jordan: we have region-specific storage; for Hosted you can choose the region and we keep audit logs in that region. Dedicated/Private give you full control.
08:21 Elena: wrap up — what do we need to sign-off on to get enterprise documentation for Crestwood?
08:27 Maya: i'll send the security pack (SOC2, ISO, penetration test summary), the KMS integration guide, and the PII scrubbing rules. Jordan will provide the 30-day scrubbed export sample and a runbook for SIEM integration. Ravi will coordinate the SIEM workshop and legal retention wording.
08:45 Jordan: action items listed in the notes. any final questions?
08:49 Elena: just one — about costs for extended retention — ballpark?
08:53 Maya: we'll include pricing tiers in the follow-up; it's typically an add-on priced by GB/month with discounts on committed volume.
08:59 Elena: thanks everyone.
09:01 End of call
